newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy calls another confidence vote on decree.
newsitem.headline: Italy calls another confidence vote on decree.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government, which on Tuesday easily won a confidence vote on a package of financial measures, has called another confidence vote to turn a decree into law, a senior member of a coalition party said.
Sergio Mattarella, leader of the centrist PPI party in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) said after a meeting of parliamentary party leaders a new confidence test would be held.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government earlier easily won a confidence vote on the final part of a package of financial measures contained in the 1997 budget designed to sweep away a host of opposition amendments.
The latest confidence vote relates to a decree on arrangements for the transport sector.
Under a ruling by the Constitutional Court, governments can no longer roll over expiring decrees and Prodi has resorted to confidence motions several times, winning with ease.
If the government loses a confidence vote it must resign.

No time for the confidence vote was immediately available. The party leaders decided that the final vote on the financial measures would be held on Wednesday, probably in the afternoon, Mattarella told reporters.
